A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphNC research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original AUROC/AUPRC experiments on six datasets, teacher-model comparisons, component ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, degraded-teacher experiments, anomaly-detection counts and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Equation (3) and Algorithm 1 change NormReg from a negative to a positive mean squared representation discrepancy. This corrects the written objective to match the minimization described in both versions. The architecture and components remain unchanged; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: All six datasets and original graph anomaly detection tasks remain. Appendix C.4 adds a supervision-corruption scenario by injecting anomalies into the teacher's labeled-normal training set.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated GADNR and ADA-GAD comparisons while retaining all seven earlier baselines. This extends the reconstruction-based comparator group; the three teacher-model choices remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The original 15% labeled-normal protocol, AUROC/AUPRC metrics and stated hyperparameters remain. New analyses introduce deliberately contaminated teacher training, true-anomaly counts, summaries grouped by teacher AUROC, and training/inference timing. The contamination rate and detection threshold are unspecified.

E4.justification: Appendices C.4–C.6 substantially expand scrutiny of teacher dependence through degraded-teacher tests, missed-anomaly recovery analysis and gains across teacher-quality ranges. Appendix E.2 adds empirical efficiency analysis. Existing ablations are retained, including v1 Table 3 reproduced as v2 Table 5.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averages over five independent runs with different random seeds. No changed repetition policy, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced. Table 8 adds grouped performance averages without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New results include baseline scores, degraded-teacher outcomes, accuracy-bin gains, detection counts and runtimes. GADNR now leads Tolokers AUPRC: 0.3511 versus GraphNC's 0.3082. GraphNC(OCGNN)'s Amazon AUPRC changes from 0.6617 in v1 Table 5 to 0.7372 in v2 Table 6. Previously reported main-comparison scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Correcting Equation (3)'s sign makes the formal NormReg definition consistent with the positive loss already used in Appendix D, Equation (8). The variance-shrinkage theorem, assumptions, proof and complexity derivation otherwise retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: Both versions present the same two-component calibration framework, claim improvements across three teacher families, and claim state-of-the-art performance on six benchmarks. The headline contributions retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: The limitation shifts from requiring a fairly good teacher to requiring at least coarse supervision, including from poor teachers. Appendices C.4–C.6 add explanations connecting robustness and missed-anomaly recovery to ScoreDA–NormReg cooperation. Section 5.4 also removes the assertion that GraphNC generally improves as labeled training size increases.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 newly reports training and inference times. v2 removes the reproducibility statement, including the assertion that source code was submitted as supplementary material. The promised code-release link and existing software, hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Roy et al. (2024), He et al. (2024) and Zhou et al. (2022), including descriptions of GADNR and ADA-GAD. The broader positioning relative to graph anomaly detection and semi-supervised learning remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed, wording and cross-references are corrected, and Algorithm 1 is rewritten more clearly. Appendix subsections are reorganized, the reproducibility statement is removed, and a generic impact statement is added. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to two columns, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Table 1 expands; Table 3 becomes a three-dataset summary with the full table retained in the appendix. Tables 7–8 and Figures 7–8 are new, while Figures 2 and 5 are revised.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes the loss-sign inconsistency and an inconsistent AUPRC entry, while additional baselines and teacher-dependence analyses strengthen empirical scrutiny. These gains are limited by missing settings for the new analyses and the retained universal-superiority statement in Section 5.1, which conflicts with GADNR's higher Tolokers AUPRC. The evidence supports a modest net improvement.
